subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 45-year-old woman is diagnosed with a mismatch repair-deficient adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic MLH1 variant, and her sister is referred for genetic counseling and cancer screening.
question: This patient is at increased risk for which of the following additional malignancies?
explanation_correct: Lynch syndrome (hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer) is caused by defective mismatch repair, classically from MLH1 or MSH2 mutations. It increases the risk of colorectal cancer (frequently right-sided) as well as endometrial, ovarian, gastric, and urothelial cancers, which is why endometrial cancer screening is recommended.

explanation_incorrect.A: Lung adenocarcinoma is not part of Lynch syndrome; tobacco exposure is the dominant risk factor.
explanation_incorrect.B: Glioblastoma is associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome and other tumor predisposition syndromes, not Lynch syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.C: Medullary thyroid carcinoma is associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2.
explanation_incorrect.D: Retinoblastoma is caused by loss of the RB1 tumor suppressor gene.

educationalObjective: Lynch syndrome predisposes to colorectal, endometrial, ovarian, gastric, and urothelial cancers because of mismatch repair deficiency.
